claim: The ANT scores alerting, orienting and conflict by subtraction; the original finding is that the three scores are nearly uncorrelated (Fan 2002), and later large samples agree (N=588: r .07, .01, -.04).
agent_test: Not testable on an LLM directly; use as a design note: keep readiness, selection, conflict checks as separate scored probes.
note_gap_search: Fan 2002 full text verified: 47/51/84 ms, retest .52/.61/.77, no significant correlations, but a significant cue x flanker interaction.
audit_note: Fan 2002 abstract and McConnell & Shore numbers (N=588 after 10 excluded, r .07/.01/-.04) verified; caveat: those r values are for trimmed RT, error-rate correlations between networks were significant (-.35, .33, -.23), and 'later large samples' is one study.

claim: Network scores do interact (alerting x flanker, validity x flanker); about half of 14 ANT studies show strong interactions, and the size depends on cue-target interval, modality and inhibition of return.
agent_test: none; background.
audit_note: Wang 2014 text says strong interactions in only half of 14 studies and names modality, SOA, IOR; Fan 2009 -13 ms, t(29)=-2.07 verified.

claim: The subtraction score is a mixed measure: executive (flanker) scores differ across the four cue types (McConnell & Shore 2011), and cue x flanker interactions mean the three networks are not fully separable, which calls the independence claim into question even though between-network score correlations stay near zero.
agent_test: none; background.
audit_note: McConnell & Shore verify that executive scores differ across cue types (t>3.3) but they and Fan 2002 still find between-network scores uncorrelated; sources show interactions and mixing, not that independence is an artefact (Wang 2014 and 2015 are one lab).
claim_before_audit: The subtraction score is a mixed measure: executive scores differ across the four cue types, so the 'independence' claim is partly an artefact of how scores are averaged.

claim: Reliability is uneven: conflict (executive) score is reliable (retest .81, split-half ~.8), alerting and orienting are poor (.20-.61 split-half, retest .36/.41 single session).
agent_test: When scoring an agent on conflict tasks, use many trials; do not rely on alerting-style differences.
audit_note: Fan 2001 retest .36/.41/.81 and MacLeod-quoted ranges (.20-.61 alerting/orienting, .65-.81 executive) verified; the .20-.61 range is 'across studies' reliability, not strictly split-half.

claim: The flanker RT cost has low test-retest reliability (ICC .40 in Hedge Study 1, .57 in Study 2) although congruent and incongruent RTs are reliable (.66-.74): robust group effects do not give reliable individual differences.
agent_test: Use paired comparisons within one agent across many items, not between-agent difference scores.
audit_note: Hedge 2018 flanker RT cost ICC .40 (S1) and .57 (S2) and S1 congruent .74/incongruent .66 verified; the .66-.74 range is Study 1 only (Study 2 .62-.69).

claim: Flanker and Stroop RT costs correlate weakly across tasks (rho=.14, disattenuated .25; Hedge et al. 2018), which is partly due to low reliability of RT-cost scores and is not evidence by itself that executive conflict is not a single construct.
agent_test: Test a scaffold on several conflict tasks, not one.
audit_note: Hedge reports flanker-Stroop RT cost rho=.14 (disattenuated .25, N~100) but says low reliability attenuates correlations and only that some relations are 'not consistent with a single underlying construct'; it does not conclude executive conflict is not one construct.
claim_before_audit: Flanker and Stroop RT costs correlate weakly across tasks (r=.14, disattenuated .25), so 'executive conflict' is not one construct.

claim: Heritability: only the conflict network showed clear heritability in twins (N=52 pairs); alerting and orienting estimates are noisy with wide intervals.
agent_test: none.

claim: Development: alerting reaches near-adult level by about age 12 (Klein 2024) and keeps changing past age 10 (Rueda 2004); orienting trajectories depend on cue informativeness and are unclear; executive conflict scores improve with age in childhood per the lifespan meta-analysis (Rueda 2004 found them stable after age 7), and all three networks still develop through adolescence. In children, ADHD minus control differences are small: alerting 13 ms, executive 13 ms, orienting about 0 (2 ms, CrI -5 to 10).
agent_test: none; background.
audit_note: ADHD-minus-control 13/13/2 ms verified, and Klein 2024 says alerting reaches near-adult level by age 12 and executive scores keep improving in childhood; but orienting 'mature by 10-12' is not supported (Rueda 2004: orienting unchanged age 6-9, conflict stable after age 7; Klein: orienting depends on cue informativeness; adolescent study: all networks keep developing to 19).
claim_before_audit: Development: alerting and orienting mature by about age 10-12; conflict keeps improving; ADHD vs control difference is small (alerting 13 ms, executive 13 ms, orienting about 0).

claim: Children show no cue x flanker interaction (F=1.03) where adults do, i.e. interaction between networks is itself developmental.
agent_test: none.
note_gap_search: Fan 2002 itself says the child pilot gave no interaction (no numbers). Rueda 2004 full text still unread.

claim: Frontier LLMs show a collapse in Stroop-style conflict as list length grows: GPT-4o incongruent colour naming 91% (5 words) to 15% (40); Claude 3.5 Sonnet 76% (20) to 24% (40); congruent stays near 99% to 20 words.
agent_test: Equal-token test: run Stroop lists of 5-40 items with and without a separate 'answer only the ink' verification pass. Note a16/b23 are the same study (paper and preprint), so independence is 1.

claim: Open 7B-72B models score 40-60% on incongruent flanker vs human 93-96%; adding explicit reasoning lifts them to 91-99% (Llama-3.1-8B .471 to .910; Qwen2-32B .638 to .985).
agent_test: Replicate flanker with and without a reasoning step at matched total tokens; check whether gain survives equal-token best-of-N.
note_gap_search: Gap 4: reasoning closes the flanker gap (Qwen2-32B incongruent 0.638 to 0.985) at thousands of tokens; does not help WCST or spans.

claim: Vision-language models show a congruency cost on conflict tasks (0.852 vs 0.567 accuracy, non-squared; Stroop-colour small cost in easy designs, big in squared/overlay designs), and extra computation reduces the gap.
agent_test: Compare extra reasoning tokens against matched sampling on overlay/Stroop VLM tasks.
audit_note: 0.852 vs 0.567, squared 0.634 vs 0.297, Stroop-colour 0.968 vs 0.931 (easy) and 0.591 vs 0.366 (squared) verified in Wang et al.; 'computation' there means parameter count (model size), not test-time compute, and the claim rests on one paper (Hu 2025 covers conflict adaptation, not the congruency cost).

claim: Conflict in VLMs is a feature competition: text dominates colour (CLIP word 97.8% vs ink about 20%; larger set 99.5% vs 15.9%), and prompt wording alone moves ink accuracy from 24% to 97%.
agent_test: Prompt-sensitivity sweep: 10 phrasings of the same conflict probe; report range, not one number.
audit_note: Teker et al. numbers verified (CLIP word 97.8% vs ink ~20%; 23,338-image set 99.5% vs 15.9%; ink accuracy 24-97% across prompt variants); Zhao et al. exists and supports text capture; the 24-97% range is quoted in the main text, only some variants (31.1%, 60%) are tabulated.

claim: In text LLMs, conflict is mechanistically localised: ablation changes incongruent probability by 0.88 but congruent by 0.10; congruent margin rises when incongruent falls (a cost-benefit trade).
agent_test: Needs open weights; not testable on a black-box scaffold.

claim: Irrelevant context hurts LLMs: GSM-IC fewer than 30% of problems solved consistently; Lost-in-the-middle mid-position accuracy falls over 20 points. Instructions to ignore help only a few points.
agent_test: Add distractors to our benchmark items; compare plain, 'ignore' instruction, and a filter-then-answer pass at equal tokens.
audit_note: Shi et al.: fewer than 30% base problems consistently solved, instruction gains 1.5-5.5 micro points (macro up to ~9 for COT, which the paper calls consistent improvement); Liu et al.: GPT-3.5 multi-doc QA can drop by more than 20% (percent not stated as points) - minor wording slips.

claim: System 2 Attention (regenerate the context without irrelevant parts) raised factuality 62.8% to 80.3% and GSM-IC by about 10-12 points; the gain over instructed prompting is inconsistent.
agent_test: Run S2A rewrite vs plain at equal tokens (the rewrite costs tokens: count them).
note_gap_search: Gap 5: no token-matched comparison found; Shi 2023 self-consistency (20 samples) is stronger on GSM-IC; S2A not tested on frontier models.
audit_note: 62.8->80.3 factuality and GSM-IC +12/+10 verified in Weston & Sukhbaatar, but the closing clause is backwards: instructed prompting gave no consistent gain over baseline (GSM-IC 54.7 vs 56.3 and 54.7 vs 51.7; factuality 71.7%), so S2A beat instructed prompting clearly (68.3/61.3 vs 54.7; 80.3 vs 71.7); Shi et al. found the ignore-instruction helped other models (code-davinci-002).

claim: Selective slow reasoning gated by an inhibition-style signal gives a small gain: 8.2% of items routed lifts accuracy 47.90% to 48.92% vs random 46.76%.
agent_test: Gate by confidence; expect about +1 point; likely not worth complexity.

claim: ANT-style analogies to LLM agents are weak: we found no study that runs a full three-network ANT (alerting, orienting, executive) on an LLM; only the executive part has been tested.
agent_test: Gap; background only.
audit_note: Patel/Wang/Fan Stroop paper tests executive conflict only (abstract) and a search found no ANT-style LLM study; this is an absence-of-evidence claim worded as 'we found no study', and listed a28 is the agent's own synthesis rather than an independent source.

claim: Cognitive-psychology batteries on LLMs are brittle to wording: GPT-3 vignettes broke under adversarial changes and CRT answered intuitively wrong.
agent_test: Report results over prompt permutations, never single prompts.
audit_note: Binz & Schulz (GPT-3: all three CRT items intuitive-wrong, adversarial vignettes e.g. cab '20%'), Han et al. (A-not-B drops up to 83.3%) and Teker prompt sensitivity verified; scope is GPT-3-era and a few other models, so the general 'batteries are brittle' headline is broader than GPT-3 evidence.

claim: Reasoning (extra thinking tokens) closes the LLM flanker gap but at high, flat cost, and does not remove semantic interference in every family: Qwen2-32B incongruent 0.638 to 0.985 with reasoning; chains of hundreds to thousands of tokens equal on congruent trials; in a symbol-arithmetic test with misleading semantics R1 fell to 40% while o1 stayed at 94%.
agent_test: Compare a verify-step prompt against a reasoning-token budget at equal tokens on a text Stroop list.

claim: Trial-history conflict adaptation appears in open VLMs: 12 of 13 models did better on an incongruent trial after another incongruent one (log probability of the correct color); the one exception sat at 100% accuracy.
agent_test: Check whether an agent scaffold that raises checking after a conflict beats a fixed schedule.

claim: For distraction in math word problems, majority vote over 20 samples beat prompting tricks on GSM-IC (+11 points micro; best macro only 45%), but at 20x the calls; an instruction to ignore irrelevant text helped older models but not LLaMA-2-70B in the S2A paper. No study matches tokens across the options.
agent_test: Run rewrite-filter vs instruction vs self-consistency at equal total tokens on a current model.

claim: Larger models resolve VLM conflict better; here 'computation' means parameter count: congruent 0.852 vs incongruent 0.567 overall, with large models falling below chance on the hardest incongruent trials. Test-time compute was not varied.
agent_test: Not applicable.

claim: In small text LLMs the conflict cost is capacity-sensitive: five-clause rule prefixes cut incongruent probability by 0.30 vs two-clause with little change on congruent trials; no prompt-wording sweep exists for text Stroop, while VLM ink accuracy ranges 24-97% with wording and format.
agent_test: Sweep 10 prompt phrasings on one text Stroop list and report the range.

claim: No LLM study of alerting (warning cue) or orienting (valid vs invalid cue) was found, nor any link between LLM conflict scores and real agent task performance, confidence under conflict, or trials needed for a stable LLM conflict score.
agent_test: Build a cue-validity probe: a hint that is right 80% or wrong 20% of the time, and score the cost of the invalid hint.
